seoTitle: Hex Color to CSS Filter: Recolor Black Icons | Free
metaDescription: Turn a hex colour into an invert, sepia, saturate, hue-rotate chain that recolours black icons, with the match error shown. Runs in your browser.
intro: Searches for a CSS filter chain that turns a black image or icon into your target colour and reports how close the result is.
why:
You cannot set the fill of an img or a CSS background icon with a colour value, but you can change its pixels with filter. Starting from black, a chain of invert, sepia, saturate, hue-rotate, brightness and contrast can reach most colours.

The tool uses the colour matrices from the CSS Filter Effects spec and a fixed-seed search, so the same colour always gives the same answer. It shows the colour the chain really produces and the largest channel error, so you see when a match is only rough. I checked five colours against Chrome canvas filters and they were within 3 of 255 per channel.
howTo: Enter a hex colour such as #1d4ed8.
Read the filter line and the colour it actually produces.
Apply the filter to a black image or icon.

faq.q: Does it work on non-black images?
faq.a: No. The chain is solved starting from pure black. For other colours, use an SVG with currentColor instead.

faq.q: Why is the match not exact?
faq.a: The search is approximate and values are rounded to whole numbers. The error is shown so you can judge.

faq.q: Will it look the same in every browser?
faq.a: Filters are specified, but small rendering differences exist. Check on your target browsers.
